extracted.intended_audience: drug manufacturers, applicants, and other persons participating in FDA rulemaking or certification/approval dockets
extracted.subtask_short: FDA antibiotic drug standards and procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule criteria and procedural requirements from the FDA Federal Register entries setting standards for new antibiotic dosage forms (identity, strength, quality, purity, labeling, sampling, assay methods) and the procedural rules for comments, hearings, and docket submissions. Also includes the FDA policy on a uniform compliance date for food labeling and environmental-impact determinations for such rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform compliance date for food labeling regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is establishing January 1, 1993 as its new uniform compliance date with all FDA final food labeling regulations that are published in the Federal Register after January 1, 1990, and before January 1, 1992.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy applies only to final FDA food labeling regulations published in that window and those regulations will specifically identify January 1, 1993 as their compliance date. Industry is encouraged to comply earlier when feasible. If special circumstances justify a different compliance date for a particular regulation, FDA will determine and specify an appropriate date when the regulation is published. This notice does not change existing requirements with previously announced compliance dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental impact determination (21 CFR 25.24(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency has determined under 21 CFR 25.24(c)(6) that this action is of a type that does not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, neither an environmental assessment nor an environmental impact statement is required for these actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting comments to Dockets Management Branch (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons may submit written comments to the Dockets Management Branch; comments must be identified with the docket number found in brackets in the heading of the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two copies of any comments are to be submitted, except that individuals may submit one copy. Received comments may be seen in the Dockets Management Branch between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and identification of copies for different submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for number of copies and identification depend on submission type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary comments: submit two copies (individuals may submit one). For submissions related to hearings/requests under specific orders: submissions must be filed in three copies, identified with the docket number appearing in the heading, and filed with the Dockets Management Branch. Submissions that are not protected from public disclosure may be inspected at the Dockets Management Branch between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a hearing—timing and required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person adversely affected by the final rule may file objections and request a hearing but must show reasonable grounds and meet filing deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File (1) on or before the specified date (e.g., February 5, 1990) a written notice of participation and request for hearing, and (2) on or before the specified later date (e.g., March 5, 1990) the data, information, and analyses on which the person relies to justify a hearing, as specified in 21 CFR 314.300. A request for hearing may not rest upon mere allegations or denials but must set forth specific facts showing a genuine and substantial issue of fact. If the request for hearing, on its face, lacks a genuine and substantial issue of fact or is not in required format or analyses, the Commissioner will enter summary judgment against the requester, making findings and denying a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of notice-and-comment for noncontroversial rules announcing accepted standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When a final rule announces standards that FDA has accepted in a request for approval and the rule is not controversial, FDA may find notice-and-comment procedure unnecessary and not in the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such final rules may become effective immediately (e.g., effective February 5, 1990) but FDA still permits interested persons to submit comments and, where appropriate, file objections and request hearings within the announced timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions under this order, except for data and information prohibited from public disclosure, may be seen in the Dockets Management Branch between 9 a.m. and 4 p.m., Monday through Friday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to comments, requests for hearing, data and analyses (unless protected by law), and other submissions identified with the docket number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity for nafcillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: Nafcillin sodium injection is a frozen, aqueous, iso-osmotic solution of nafcillin sodium which may contain one or more suitable and harmless buffer substances and a tonicity adjusting agent. Each milliliter contains nafcillin sodium equivalent to 20 or 40 milligrams of nafcillin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nafcillin content is satisfactory if it is not less than 90 percent and not more than 120 percent of the number of milligrams represented. It must be sterile, nonpyrogenic, and have pH not less than 6.0 and not more than 8.5. The nafcillin sodium monohydrate used must conform to standards prescribed by § 440.41(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirement for nafcillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: The drug shall be labeled in accordance with the requirements of § 432.5 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, this drug shall be labeled 'nafcillin sodium injection.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for certification and sample/data submissions for nafcillin
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for certification must comply with thaw requirements of § 431.1 and contain results of tests/assays and samples as required by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required test results: (i)(A) tests/assays on the nafcillin sodium monohydrate used in making the batch for potency, moisture, pH, crystallinity, nafcillin content and identity; (i)(B) tests on the batch for nafcillin content, sterility, pyrogens, and pH. Samples, if required: (A) the monohydrate used—10 packages ~300 mg each; (B) the batch—minimum of 10 immediate containers for all tests except sterility and 20 immediate containers for sterility testing, collected at regular intervals throughout each filling operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests and methods of assay for nafcillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific assay and test methods to establish conformity for nafcillin sodium injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nafcillin content: proceed as directed in § 440.241a(b)(1), except use the thawed solution. Sterility: proceed as directed in § 436.20 of this chapter using the method described in paragraph (e)(1) of that section. Pyrogens: proceed as directed in § 436.32(a), except inject a sufficient volume of the undiluted solution to deliver 80 milligrams of nafcillin per kilogram. pH: proceed as directed in § 436.202 using the undiluted solution. The sample solution used for testing must be at room temperature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity for oxacillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: Oxacillin sodium injection is a frozen aqueous, iso-osmotic solution of oxacillin sodium which may contain buffer substances and a tonicity adjusting agent. Each milliliter contains oxacillin sodium equivalent to 20 or 40 milligrams of oxacillin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oxacillin content is satisfactory if not less than 90 percent and not more than 115 percent of the represented milligrams. It must be sterile, nonpyrogenic, and have pH not less than 6.0 and not more than 8.5. The oxacillin sodium monohydrate used must conform to § 440.49(a)(1), except that the pH of an aqueous solution containing 30 milligrams per milliliter is not less than 4.0 and not more than 7.0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirement for oxacillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: The drug shall be labeled in accordance with the requirements of § 432.5 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, this drug shall be labeled 'oxacillin sodium injection.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for certification and sample/data submissions for oxacillin
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for certification must comply with § 431.1 and contain results of tests/assays on the oxacillin sodium monohydrate and the batch, and samples if required by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required test results: (i)(A) monohydrate used in making the batch—potency, moisture, pH, oxacillin content, crystallinity, and identity; (i)(B) the batch—oxacillin content, sterility, pyrogens, and pH. Samples: (A) monohydrate—10 packages ~300 mg each; (B) batch—minimum of 10 immediate containers for all tests except sterility and 20 immediate containers for sterility testing collected at regular intervals throughout each filling operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests and methods of assay for oxacillin sodium injection
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified assay and test methods for oxacillin sodium injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oxacillin content: proceed as directed in § 440.249a(b)(1), except use the thawed solution. Sterility: proceed as directed in § 436.20 using the method described in paragraph (e)(1). Pyrogens: proceed as directed in § 436.32(a), except inject a sufficient volume of the undiluted solution to deliver 20 milligrams of oxacillin per kilogram. pH: proceed as directed in § 438.202 using the undiluted solution. The sample solution used for testing must be at room temperature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity for erythromycin estolate and sulfisoxazole acetyl oral suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Erythromycin estolate and sulfisoxazole acetyl oral suspension is erythromycin estolate and sulfisoxazole acetyl with suitable and harmless buffer substances, preservatives, solvents, stabilizers, emulsifiers, dispersing agents, colorings, and flavorings. Each milliliter contains erythromycin estolate equivalent to 25 milligrams of erythromycin and 120 milligrams of sulfisoxazole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erythromycin content is satisfactory if not less than 90 percent and not more than 120 percent of the represented milligrams. Sulfisoxazole acetyl content is satisfactory if not less than 90 percent and not more than 115 percent of the represented milligrams. pH must be not less than 3.5 and not more than 6.5. The erythromycin estolate used must conform to § 452.15(a)(1) and the sulfisoxazole acetyl used must conform to the U.S.P. XXII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling requirement for erythromycin estolate and sulfisoxazole acetyl oral suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The drug shall be labeled in accordance with the requirements of § 432.5 of this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for certification and sample/data submissions for erythromycin/sulfisoxazole suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Each request for certification must comply with § 431.1 and contain results of tests/assays on the ingredients and the batch, and samples if required by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required test results: (i)(A) erythromycin estolate used in making the batch—potency, moisture, pH, crystallinity, and identity; (i)(B) sulfisoxazole acetyl used in making the batch—for all U.S.P. XXII specifications; (i)(C) the batch—for erythromycin content, sulfisoxazole content, and pH. Samples, if required: (A) erythromycin estolate used in making the batch—10 packages each containing not less than 500 milligrams; (B) the batch—a minimum of 15 immediate containers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests and methods of assay for erythromycin estolate and sulfisoxazole acetyl suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified assay procedures for erythromycin and sulfisoxazole content and pH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erythromycin content: proceed as directed in § 436.105, preparing the sample by removing a representative volume, diluting with methyl alcohol to ~2.5 mg/mL (estimated), then diluting with 0.1M potassium phosphate buffer pH 8.0 to ~1.0 mg/mL, hydrolyze in 60°C water bath for 2 hours or at room temperature for 16–18 hours, then dilute to reference concentration of 1.0 µg/mL (estimated). Sulfisoxazole content: proceed as directed in § 436.328. pH: proceed as directed in § 436.202 using the drug as prepared for dispensing.
